claim: A non-breaching party may recover consequential damages for lost downstream contracts only where such losses were reasonably foreseeable to both parties at the time the original agreement was executed. The Seventh Circuit in Thatcher held that foreseeability cannot be established by mere industry custom alone without specific contractual language or prior course of dealing.
citation: Thatcher v. Ironwood Supply Group, 887 F.2d 341 (7th Cir. 1991)
initial_reasoning: In Thatcher v. Ironwood Supply Group, 887 F.2d 341 (7th Cir. 1991), the Seventh Circuit held that a non‑breaching party may recover consequential damages for lost downstream contracts only when such losses were reasonably foreseeable to both parties at the time of the agreement, and that foreseeability cannot be inferred solely from industry custom without specific contractual language or a prior course of dealing. This directly supports the claim.
